items.name: Shabbat (שַׁבָּת)
items.subtitle: Every week — Friday evening to Saturday evening
items.description: The weekly Sabbath, based on Creation (Genesis 2:3) and the Law (Exodus 20:8-11). Total cessation of work, festive meals, synagogue. Symbolizes the Covenant between God and Israel (Exodus 31:13). The halakha lists 39 categories of prohibited work.
items.detail: Duration: 25 hours. Starts with the woman lighting the candles. Ends with Havdalah (separation).

items.name: Passover — Pesah (פֶּסַח)
items.subtitle: 14-21 Nissan (March-April)
items.description: Commemoration of the Exodus from Egypt (Exodus 12). Seder meal with Passover lamb, bitter herbs, matzot (unleavened bread). Reading the Haggadah. Houses are cleansed of all leaven (hametz) — a symbol of sin and pride.
items.detail: Duration: 7 days (8 in diaspora). The 4 cups of wine symbolize the 4 divine promises of Exodus 6:6-7.

items.name: Pentecost — Shavuot (שָׁבוּעוֹת)
items.subtitle: 6-7 Sivan (May-June) — 50 days after Passover
items.description: Festival of Weeks/Harvest. Commemoration of the gift of the Torah at Sinai. Offering of the first fruits (bikourim). We read the book of Ruth. In NT: the day of Pentecost (Acts 2) falls on this day.
items.detail: Duration: 1 day (2 in diaspora). The synagogue is decorated with greenery evoking Mount Sinai.

items.name: Rosh Hashanah (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה)
items.subtitle: 1-2 Tishri (September-October)
items.description: Jewish New Year — literally 'head of the year'. Symbolic divine judgment: God opens the Books of life. Sound of the Shofar (ram's horn) 100 times. Period of repentance (Yamim Noraim). Honey and apple for a 'happy new year'.
items.detail: Duration: 2 days. Begins 10 days of penance which ends on Yom Kippur.

items.name: Yom Kippur (יוֹם כִּפּוּר)
items.subtitle: 10 Tishri — Great Day of Atonement
items.description: Most solemn day of the Jewish year. 25-hour fast, five prayer services, collective confessions. At the time of the Temple: the High Priest enters once a year into the Holy of Holies to sprinkle the mercy seat with blood (Leviticus 16). The scapegoat is sent to the desert.
items.detail: Prohibited: eating, drinking, washing, marital relations, perfume, leather shoes.

items.name: Sukkot (סֻכּוֹת)
items.subtitle: 15-21 Tishri — Festival of Cabins
items.description: Commemorating 40 years in the desert. Construction of huts (sukkot) with green roofs revealing the sky. We eat there, pray, sometimes sleep for 7 days. The 4 species: loulav (palm tree), etrog (citron), myrtle, willow — moved towards the 4 cardinal points.
items.detail: The happiest holiday. The 7th day (Hoshana Rabba) is the day of final closure of judgment.

items.name: Hanukkah (חֲנֻכָּה)
items.subtitle: 25 Kislev — 8 days (November-December)
items.description: Festival of Lights — commemoration of the rededication of the Temple (165 BC) after the victory of the Maccabees over Antiochos IV. Oil miracle (1 day oil burns 8 days). Lighting of Hanoukia (9-branched candlestick), dreidel games, donuts.
items.detail: Non-biblical (inter-testamental). Mentioned in John 10:22 ('Feast of Dedication').

items.name: Purim (פּוּרִים)
items.subtitle: 14 Adar (February-March)
items.description: Most joyous holiday — commemoration of the salvation of the Jews in Persia (book of Esther). Reading of the Megilah (book of Esther) in synagogue. Noise is made in the name of Haman. Costumes, feasts, gifts of food (mishloah manot), donations to the poor.
items.detail: Duration: 1 day. 'Purim' = drawing of lots — Haman cast lots to choose the day of the massacre.

items.name: Jubilee Year (יוֹבֵל)
items.subtitle: Every 50 years
items.description: After 7 weeks of years (49 years), the year 50 is the Jubilee (Leviticus 25). Liberation of all Hebrew slaves, return of each family to their ancestral land, forgiveness of debts. Sounding of the Shofar on Yom Kippur of the Jubilee Year. Jesus quotes Isaiah 61 ('the year of grace') at the beginning of his ministry.
items.detail: The Sabbatical Year (every 7 years) precedes the Jubilee: the earth rests, debts are forgiven.

items.name: Nissan (נִיסָן)
items.subtitle: 1st sacred month — March/April
items.description: First month of the liturgical calendar. Month of Passover (Pesach). Exodus 12:2: 'This month shall be the beginning of months for you, and the first of months of the year for you.' Month of deliverance and miracles.
items.detail: 30 days. Start of spring. The windfall stopped on the 16th of Nissan.

items.name: Iyar (אִיָּר)
items.subtitle: 2nd month — April/May
items.description: Month of healing (initial letters = Ani YHWH Ropheka — 'I am the Lord who heals you'). Pesah Sheni (Secondary Passover) on 14 Iyar for those who had been impure.
items.detail: 29 days. Counting of the Omer continues.

items.name: Sivan (סִיוָן)
items.subtitle: 3rd month — May/June
items.description: Month of the giving of the Torah at Sinai. Feast of Shavuot (Pentecost) on Sivan 6. Month linked to divine revelation and the Law.
items.detail: 30 days. In NT: Pentecost of Acts 2 falls this month.

items.name: Tammuz (תַּמּוּז)
items.subtitle: 4th month — June/July
items.description: Month of mourning — on Tammuz 17, Moses breaks the Tables of the Law. Beginning of the 3-week period of mourning leading to 9 Av.

items.name: Av (אָב)
items.subtitle: 5th month — July/August
items.description: Saddest month. The 9th of Av (Ticha B'Av): destruction of the 1st Temple (586 BC) and the 2nd Temple (70 AD), expulsion from Spain (1492), and numerous Jewish tragedies. 25 hour fast.
items.detail: 30 days. The 15th of Av is paradoxically a joyous holiday (feast of love).

items.name: Elul (אֱלוּל)
items.subtitle: 6th month — August/September
items.description: Month of repentance preceding Rosh Hashanah. The Shofar is blown every morning. The king is in the field — image of God's closeness to his people before judgment.

items.name: Tishri
items.subtitle: 7th month — September/October
items.description: Holiest month — Rosh Hashanah (1-2), Yom Kippur (10), Sukkot (15-21), Shemini Atzeret (22), Simchat Torah (23). Month 7 reflects the perfection of the number 7.
items.detail: 30 days. Start of the calendar year (although 7th liturgical month).

items.name: Heshvan (חֶשְׁוָן)
items.subtitle: 8th month — October/November
items.description: Only month without a party. Sometimes called 'Mar-Cheshvan' (Bitter Cheshvan). Tradition says that the dedication of Solomon's Temple was to take place there. Rainy month in Israel — the flood began on Cheshvan 17.

items.name: Kislev
items.subtitle: 9th month — November/December
items.description: Month of Hanukkah (25 Kislev). In some traditions, months of dreams and visions (dreams of Joseph, vision of Zechariah). Kislev 19 is the Hasidic New Year.

items.name: Tevet (טֵבֵת)
items.subtitle: 10th month — December/January
items.description: Tevet 8: Ptolemy II translated the Torah into Greek (Septuagint) — fasted by some. Tevet 10: start of the siege of Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar.

items.name: Shevat (שְׁבָט)
items.subtitle: 11th month — January/February
items.description: The 15th of Shevat: Rosh Hashanah LaIlanot — New Year of Trees (Tu BiShvat). Reforestation, tasting of the 7 species of Israel. Almond trees are blooming in Israel.

items.name: Adar (אֲדָר)
items.subtitle: 12th month — February/March
items.description: Happiest month. Purim on Adar 14. Saying: 'When Adar enters, joy increases.' Month of birth and death of Moses (7 Adar).
items.detail: 29 days. Leap years: Adar I (30d) + Adar II (29d).

items.name: Guera (גֵּרָה)
items.subtitle: Smallest monetary unit
items.description: 1/20 of a century. The smallest currency mentioned in the Torah. Used for the census half-century.

items.name: Beka (בֶּקַע)
items.subtitle: Half shekel
items.description: Equivalent to 10 gueras = 1/2 shekel. Used in the first census of Israel (Exodus 38:26). Weighs approximately 5-6 grams.

items.name: Shekel (שֶׁקֶל)
items.subtitle: Base unit — ~11-14g silver
items.description: Fundamental monetary unit of the Hebrew Bible. The 'sanctuary shekel' is slightly heavier. Abraham weighs 400 shekels of silver to buy the cave of Machpelah (Genesis 23). Joseph sold for 20 shekels of silver.
items.detail: 1 shekel = 20 gueras = 2 bekas. Judah sold Jesus for 30 shekels (the price of a slave, Exodus 21:32).

items.name: Mine (מָנֶה)
items.subtitle: 50 shekels
items.description: Intermediate unit. 1 mina = 50 shekels (common usage) or 60 shekels (Babylonian standard). Used in important trade and in the description of the Temple of Ezekiel.

items.name: Talent
items.subtitle: 3,000 shekels = 60 minas
items.description: The largest unit of weight/value. A talent of gold was a colossal fortune — approximately 34 kg of gold or silver. David collects 3,000 talents of gold for the construction of the Temple. The parable of the talents (Matthew 25) uses this value.

items.name: Roman denarius (דִּינָר)
items.subtitle: NT times — daily wage
items.description: At the time of Jesus, the denarius (denarius) was the common currency of the Roman Empire. One denarius = 1 day of work for a farm worker (Matthew 20:2). Jesus asks to see a denarius during the tax controversy (Matthew 22:19).
items.detail: The Greek drachma had a similar value. 100 deniers = approximately 1 mine.

items.name: Guera (גֵּרָה)
items.subtitle: Weight ~0.57g
items.description: The smallest unit of weight. 20 gueras = 1 shekel.

items.name: Shekel (שֶׁקֶל)
items.subtitle: ~11.4g (shrine ~14g)
items.description: Basic unit of weight. The 'shekel of the sanctuary' is slightly higher. Weight used on scales to weigh silver, gold and precious materials.

items.name: Mine (מָנֶה)
items.subtitle: 50 shekels = ~570g
items.description: Intermediate business unit. Used in large trades.

items.name: Talent
items.subtitle: 3,000 shekels = ~34 kg
items.description: Heaviest weight. A talent of gold or silver represents a fortune. The Hailstone of Revelation weighs one talent (Rev. 16:21).

items.name: Finger (אֶצְבַּע)
items.subtitle: ~1.85cm
items.description: The smallest unit of biblical length. 4 fingers = 1 palm.

items.name: Palm / Palm (טֶפַח)
items.subtitle: ~7.4cm
items.description: 4 fingers side by side. 3 fins = 1 span.

items.name: Empan (זֶרֶת)
items.subtitle: ~22cm
items.description: Distance between extended thumb and little finger. 2 spans = 1 cubit.

items.name: Cubit (אַמָּה)
items.subtitle: ~44-52cm
items.description: Distance from elbow to fingertips. Main architectural unit of the Bible. Noah's Ark: 300 × 50 × 30 cubits. Solomon's Temple: 60 × 20 × 30 cubits.
items.detail: Genesis 6:15; 1 Kings 6:2; Ezekiel uses the 'great cubit' of 52 cm.

items.name: Door (cane, קָנֶה)
items.subtitle: 6 cubits = ~2.6 m
items.description: Used by Ezekiel to measure the eschatological Temple. The angelic measure of the Temple of Revelation (11:1).

items.name: Stadium (stádion)
items.subtitle: ~185 m (Greek)
items.description: Greek measurement used in the NT. Emmaus is 60 stadia from Jerusalem (Luke 24:13 ≈ 11 km). The New Jerusalem: 12,000 furlongs aside (Rev. 21:16).

items.name: Roman mile / League
items.subtitle: ~1,480m
items.description: The Roman mile (miliarium) = 1,000 double steps = ~1.48 km. Jesus said, 'If anyone forces you to go a mile, go with him two' (Matthew 5:41).

items.name: Sabbath (sabbath path)
items.subtitle: ~900m
items.description: Maximum distance allowed for walking on the Sabbath according to rabbinical tradition (based on Numbers 35:5). The Mount of Olives is a 'Sabbath way' from Jerusalem.

items.name: Log (לֹג)
items.subtitle: ~0.31 liters
items.description: The smallest measure of liquid volume. 4 logs = 1 kav. Used for oil in purification laws.

items.name: Kav (קַב)
items.subtitle: ~1.2 liters
items.description: Small dry measure. During the siege of Samaria, a kav of pigeon droppings sold for 5 shekels of silver (extreme famine, 2 Kings 6:25).

items.name: Omer (עֹמֶר)
items.subtitle: ~2.2 liters = 1/10 of an epha
items.description: The daily ration of manna per person (Exodus 16:16). Unity of the Feast of the First Sheaf (Leviticus 23:10-11).

items.name: Seah (סְאָה)
items.subtitle: ~7 liters = 1/3 of an epha
items.description: Sarah prepares 3 seah of flour for Abraham's 3 visitors (Genesis 18:6). The woman hides the leaven in 3 seah of flour (Matthew 13:33).

items.name: Ephah (אֵיפָה)
items.subtitle: ~22 liters
items.description: Main unit of dry measurement. The bushel = 1/10 of an ephah. Used for grain offerings (Leviticus 5:11). Must be righteous: 'Thou shalt have but one righteous ephah' (Leviticus 19:36).

items.name: Hin (הִין)
items.subtitle: ~4 liters (liquid)
items.description: Liquid equivalent of epha. Used to measure oil and wine for libations. 1 hr = 12 logs.

items.name: Bath (בַּת)
items.subtitle: ~22 liters (= ephah)
items.description: Primary liquid standard. 10 baths = 1 kor (homer). The brazen sea of ​​Solomon's Temple contained 2,000 baths (1 Kings 7:26).

items.name: Homer / Kor
items.subtitle: ~220 liters = 10 ephas
items.description: The largest measurement of volume. Quails in the desert: the people collected at least 10 homers (Numbers 11:32). Ezekiel 45:14: 10 baths = 1 homer.

items.name: 1 — Divine Oneness (אֶחָד)
items.subtitle: The One, the one, the unique
items.description: The absolute unity of God: 'Hear Israel, the LORD our God, the LORD is One' (Deuteronomy 6:4—the Shema). The number 1 expresses the incomparability of God, the exclusivity of the Alliance. There is no other god. In the NT: 'There is one God, and one Mediator' (1 Timothy 2:5).

items.name: 2 — Testimony & Duality
items.subtitle: The confirmation, the two witnesses
items.description: The Law requires 2 or 3 witnesses to establish a fact (Deuteronomy 19:15). Jesus sends his disciples out 2 by 2 (Mark 6:7). The 2 Tablets of the Law. The 2 Testaments. The 2 cherubim on the Ark. The Apocalypse speaks of the 2 witnesses (Rev. 11). 2 can also symbolize the division: good/evil, light/darkness.

items.name: 3 — Trinity & Divine Fullness
items.subtitle: Heavenly completeness
items.description: The number of divine fullness. 3 patriarchs (Abraham, Isaac, Jacob). 3 annual pilgrimages. 3 sections of the Temple (courtyard, holy place, Holy of Holies). 3 days of Jonah and the resurrection of Jesus. The Trisagion: 'Holy, Holy, Holy' (Isaiah 6:3). The daily Jewish prayer is said 3 times.

items.name: 4 — Universality & Creation
items.subtitle: The 4 corners of the earth
items.description: 4 cardinal points = the universality of the created world. 4 winds, 4 rivers of paradise (Genesis 2:10-14), 4 living beings of the divine chariot (Ezekiel 1; Revelation 4). The 4 species of Sukkot agitated towards the 4 directions. The 4 kingdoms of Daniel. The 4 Gospels.

items.name: 5 — Grace & Torah
items.subtitle: The 5 books of Moses
items.description: 5 = the 5 books of the Torah (Pentateuch). 5 = grace in Hebrew (ḥen). The 5 offerings of Leviticus. David chose 5 smooth stones against Goliath (1 Samuel 17:40). The 5 porches of Bethesda (John 5:2). The 5 loaves of multiplication (Matthew 14:17).

items.name: 6 — Imperfection & Human Work
items.subtitle: The number of man
items.description: 6 days of work (before the Sabbath). Man created on the 6th day. 6 cities of refuge. Goliath measures 6 cubits and 1 span, has 6 weapons. 666 (Revelation 13:18) = imperfection brought to its height, the triple 6 symbolizing the man who claims to replace God (7) without ever reaching him.

items.name: 7 — Perfection & Covenant
items.subtitle: The sacred number par excellence
items.description: 'Sheva' (7) shares the root of 'oath' (shevua) — in Hebrew, to swear is 'to bind by the 7'. 7 days of Creation, 7 feasts, 7 candles of the Menorah, 7 sabbatical years, 7 times forgiving × 70 (Matthew 18:22). Revelation uses 7 more than 50 times (seals, trumpets, vials, letters, spirits). 777 = absolute fullness.

items.name: 8 — New beginning
items.subtitle: Beyond the cycle of 7
items.description: 8 = the first day after the complete Sabbath = resurrection, new creation. Circumcision on the 8th day (Genesis 17:12) = entry into the Covenant, new beginning. Jesus resurrects on the first day of the week = the symbolic 8th day. The 8 people saved in the ark (1 Peter 3:20). The Hanukkah Menorah has 8 branches.

items.name: 10 — Law & Integrity
items.subtitle: The decimal of completeness
items.description: 10 Commandments, 10 plagues of Egypt, 10 generations from Noah to Abraham, 10 generations from Abraham to Noah. The tithe = 1/10. The synagogal minyan = 10 adult men (prayer quorum). The 10 virgins (Matthew 25). The 10 strings of David's harp.

items.name: 12 — Divine government
items.subtitle: The number of God's people
items.description: 12 sons of Jacob = 12 tribes of Israel. 12 apostles. 12 months of the year. 12 loaves of presence (1 per tribe). 12 pectoral stones. 12 springs in Elim (Exodus 15:27). The New Jerusalem: 12 gates, 12 foundations, 12,000 stadiums on each side, 144,000 elect (12×12×1,000).

items.name: 17 — Victory & Grace
items.subtitle: 7 + 10 = perfection of the Fa
items.description: Little known but rich number: sum of 10 (Law) and 7 (completeness). Joseph was sold at age 17 — the beginning of his path to victory. Noah's ark stops on the 17th day of the 7th month (Genesis 8:4). In the NT, Romans 8 — the victory chapter — lists 17 things that do not separate from the love of God.

items.name: 40 — Trial & Transformation
items.subtitle: The duration of the purification periods
items.description: 40 days of the flood. 40 years in the desert. 40 days of Moses at Sinai (twice). 40 days of Elijah in the desert. 40 years of the reign of David and Solomon. 40 days of temptation of Jesus. 40 days between Resurrection and Ascension. 40 = a complete time of trial leading to a transformation.

items.name: 50 — Jubilee & Pentecost
items.subtitle: Grace at the top
items.description: 50 years = the Jubilee (universal liberation, handing over of lands, Leviticus 25). 50 days between Passover and Shavuot = Pentecost. 50 columns in the courtyard of the Tabernacle. 50 clasps of gold and brass connecting the panels of the Tabernacle. The Christian Pentecost (Acts 2) falls exactly 50 days after Easter.

items.name: 70 — Nations & Expanded Fullness
items.subtitle: The universality of salvation
items.description: 70 nations from the Table of Nations (Genesis 10) = all humanity. 70 elders of Israel. 70 years of Babylonian exile (Jeremiah 25:11). 70 weeks of Daniel (9:24). Jesus sends 70 disciples (Luke 10:1)—one for each nation. 70 members of the Sanhedrin. 70 souls from the house of Jacob in Egypt.

items.name: 153 — The Great Fishes
items.subtitle: Mysterious Number of John 21
items.description: John 21:11: the miraculous catch after the Resurrection = exactly 153 large fish. The Fathers of the Church speculated a lot: Jerome said that there were 153 known species of fish = fishing symbolizes all the peoples of the earth. Mathematically: 153 = 1³+5³+3³ and the sum from 1 to 17.

items.name: 666 — The Number of the Beast
items.subtitle: Triple human imperfection
items.description: Revelation 13:18: 'The number of the beast... is the number of a man, and his number is 666.' In gematria (Hebrew numerology), 666 corresponds to 'Neron Caesar' in Hebrew — a probable allusion to Roman persecution. Symbolically: the 6 repeated 3 times = the man (6) who wants to achieve divine perfection (7) without ever achieving it.
items.detail: Revelation 13:18; 1 Kings 10:14 (666 talents of Solomon's gold)

items.name: 3 — Trinity & Divine Fullness
items.subtitle: Number of divine completeness
items.description: The number 3 expresses divine fullness: 3 patriarchs (Abraham, Isaac, Jacob), 3 divisions of the Temple, 3 obligatory annual pilgrimages, 3 days of resurrection of Jonah and Jesus. The Trisagion: 'Holy, Holy, Holy' (Isaiah 6:3).

items.name: 7 — Perfection & Covenant
items.subtitle: Number of achievement
items.description: The most symbolic number in the Bible. 7 days of Creation, 7 annual festivals, 7 candles of the Menorah, 7 sabbatical years, 70 weeks of Daniel. 'Sheva' (7) shares the root of 'oath' (shevua) — to swear by the 7.
items.detail: Revelation: 7 seals, 7 trumpets, 7 vials. 777 = absolute fullness.

items.name: 10 — Law & Integrity
items.subtitle: Decimal of completeness
items.description: 10 Commandments, 10 plagues of Egypt, 10 generations from Noah to Abraham. The tithe = 1/10. A synagogal quorum (minyan) = 10 adult men. The 10 virgins of the parable.

items.name: 12 — Divine government
items.subtitle: Number of God's people
items.description: 12 sons of Jacob = 12 tribes of Israel. 12 apostles. 12 months. 12 loaves of presence. 12 pectoral stones. The New Jerusalem: 12 gates, 12 foundations, 12,000 stadia on each side, 144,000 (12×12×1000).

items.name: 40 — Trial & Transformation
items.subtitle: Duration of probation periods
items.description: 40 days of the flood, 40 years in the desert, 40 days of Moses at Sinai, 40 years of the reign of David and Solomon, 40 days of fasting of Elijah, 40 days of temptation of Jesus, 40 days between Resurrection and Ascension.

items.name: 50 — Jubilee & Grace
items.subtitle: Number of release
items.description: 50 years = Jubilee (liberation, handover of land). 50 days between Passover and Shavuot = Pentecost. The 50 columns of the Tabernacle. Christian Pentecost = outpouring of the Spirit after 50 days.

items.name: 70 — Nations & Extended Completeness
items.subtitle: Number of national fullness
items.description: 70 nations from the Table of Nations (Genesis 10). 70 elders of Israel (Exodus 24:1). 70 years of Babylonian exile. 70 weeks of Daniel. Jesus sends 70 disciples (Luke 10). 70 members of the Sanhedrin.

items.name: Ten (עֲשָׂרָה)
items.subtitle: Basic military and social unit
items.description: The smallest unit of social organization. Jethro advises Moses to organize the people into units of 10 (Exodus 18:21). Chief of ten = lowest officer in Israel's military hierarchy. The synagogue minyan = 10.

items.name: Fifty (חֲמִשִּׁים)
items.subtitle: Group of 50 people
items.description: Intermediate unit in Moses' military organization. The leaders of fifty supervised 5 tens. Elijah is confronted by two groups of 50 soldiers sent by King Ahaziah (2 Kings 1:9-14).

items.name: Hundred (מֵאָה)
items.subtitle: Group of 100 people
items.description: Important unit in the organization of Israel. The leaders of the hundred are mentioned in the organization of the army and the nation. Jesus seated the crowd in groups of 50 and 100 (Mark 6:40).

items.name: Thousand (אֶלֶף)
items.subtitle: Tribe/clan/unit of 1000
items.description: 'Elef' = thousand, but also 'clan' or 'tribe' in certain contexts. Tribes were divided into thousands for military censuses. Leader of a thousand = senior officer. Gideon said: 'My clan is the weakest...I am the last in my father's house.'

items.name: Myriad (רְבָבָה)
items.subtitle: 10,000 — number of the innumerable
items.description: 10,000 — the largest common number in ancient Hebrew numeration. Expresses the immensity: 'Moses had 10,000 times 10,000 children of Israel' (idiom of abundance). David: 'Saul killed a thousand, and David ten thousand' (1 Samuel 18:7).

items.name: Time (שָׁעָה)
items.subtitle: 1/12 of day or night
items.description: The Hebrews divided the day (sunrise to sunset) into 12 hours of varying length depending on the season. The 'third hour' = 9 a.m., the 'sixth hour' = noon, the 'ninth hour' = 3 p.m. (time of prayer and death of Jesus).

items.name: Watch (אַשְׁמוּרָה)
items.subtitle: Division of the night into 3 or 4 parts
items.description: The night was divided into military vigils. The Hebrew OT uses 3 watches: evening watch, midnight watch, morning watch. The Roman NT uses 4 watches: evening, midnight, cockcrow, morning. Jesus walks on water in the 4th watch (Matthew 14:25).

items.name: Sabbatical Week (שְׁמִטָּה)
items.subtitle: 7 year cycle
items.description: Every 7 years, the earth rests (Leviticus 25:1-7): no sowing or harvest. Debts owed to the Israelites are forgiven (Deuteronomy 15:1-3). The Hebrew slaves are freed (Exodus 21:2). Failure to observe these sabbatical years is one of the causes of the Babylonian exile (2 Chronicles 36:21).

items.name: Generation (דּוֹר)
items.subtitle: ~40 years in the Bible
items.description: One biblical generation = approximately 40 years (the 40 years in the desert = one generation). Matthew 1:17 structures the genealogy of Jesus into 3 × 14 generations. 'Unto the 3rd and 4th generation' (punishment) vs 'unto a thousand generations' (blessing, Exodus 20:5-6).

items.name: Touniqa / Kétonet (כֻּתֹּנֶת)
items.subtitle: Long tunic — basic garment
items.description: Long shirt worn next to the skin by men and women. Could be linen (priests) or wool. Joseph receives the famous 'tunic of many colors' (or long-sleeved, ketonet passim) from his father Jacob.

items.name: Cloak / Simlah (שִׂמְלָה)
items.subtitle: Large rectangular coat
items.description: Rectangular piece of fabric worn over the tunic. Also served as a cover at night. The Law forbids keeping the poor man's cloak as a pledge after sunset (Exodus 22:25-26).

items.name: Meil (מְעִיל)
items.subtitle: Sleeveless dress, bridesmaid dress
items.description: Ceremonial clothing worn by people of high rank. Samuel wore a better one. Saul tears up Samuel's eye (1 Samuel 15:27)—symbol of the torn kingdom. David dances in meil (2 Samuel 6:14).

items.name: Belt / Hagora (חֲגוֹרָה)
items.subtitle: Belt, belt
items.description: Essential accessory for rolling up the tunic when working or fighting. 'Gird one's loins' = prepare oneself for action. John the Baptist wears a leather belt (Matthew 3:4).

items.name: Sandals (סַנְדָּל)
items.subtitle: Leather shoes
items.description: The Hebrews wore leather sandals — soles tied with laces. Taking off one's sandal = giving up a right (Ruth 4:7) or sign of unworthiness (John 1:27). God said to Moses, 'Take off your sandals' (Exodus 3:5).
items.detail: Amos 2:6 (sold for a pair of sandals)

items.name: Tzitsit (צִיצִית)
items.subtitle: Ritual fringes at the corners of the garment
items.description: Numbers 15:38-39 commands tying fringes (tzitsit) to the four corners of the garment with blue thread (tekhelet). Reminder of all the commandments. The bleeding woman touches the 'edge of Jesus' garment' (tsitsit).

items.name: Phylacteries / Tefillin (תְּפִלִּין)
items.subtitle: Leather boxes containing biblical texts
items.description: Small black leather boxes worn on the left arm and forehead during morning prayers (except Shabbat). Contain 4 passages from the Torah (Ex.13:1-10; Ex.13:11-16; Dt.6:4-9; Dt.11:13-21). Based on Deuteronomy 6:8.

items.name: Linen Breeches (מִכְנָסַיִם)
items.subtitle: Obligatory priestly underwear
items.description: White linen pants covering from the kidneys to the thighs. All priests wore them to cover their nudity during service at the altar. Reminder of holiness and modesty before God.

items.name: Linen tunic (כֻּתֹּנֶת בַּד)
items.subtitle: Long white linen robe — ordinary priests
items.description: Embroidered white tunic worn by all priests. White linen symbolizes purity. It goes down to the feet. For ordinary priests, it is the most visible garment.

items.name: Embroidered belt (אַבְנֵט)
items.subtitle: Multicolored linen belt
items.description: Belt of fine white linen with colored threads (blue, purple, crimson) worn by ordinary priests, and even more ornate for the High Priest. It allowed the tunic to be rolled up.

items.name: Miter / Turban (מִגְבָּעָה)
items.subtitle: Headgear of ordinary priests
items.description: White linen cap for ordinary priests. Different from the great turban (mitznefet) of the High Priest. Sign of sacred service and priestly dignity.

items.name: — GARMENTS OF THE HIGH PRIEST —
items.subtitle: 8 garments in total (the 4 of the priests + 4 additional)

items.name: Blue dress
items.subtitle: All-blue dress — under the Ephod
items.description: Seamless blue wool dress (tekhelet), with a border of pomegranates in alternating colored threads with gold bells. The bells jingled to signal the presence of the High Priest in the holy place.
items.detail: Exodus 28:31-35 — 'so that he may not die'

items.name: Ephod (אֵפוֹד)
items.subtitle: Supreme Priestly Apron — linen and gold
items.description: Distinctive vestment of the High Priest, made of gold thread, blue, purple, crimson wool and fine woven linen. Worn on the chest like a corselet apron. Two onyx stones on the shoulder boards bear the names of the 12 tribes (6 per side).
items.detail: Exodus 28:6-14 — The High Priest 'brings' Israel before God

items.name: Breastplate of Judgment (חֹשֶׁן)
items.subtitle: 12 precious stones — 12 tribes
items.description: Square piece (22×22 cm) of the same fabric as the Ephod, worn on the chest. Set with 12 precious stones in 4 rows, each engraved with the name of a tribe of Israel. Contained the Ourim and Tummim.
items.detail: Exodus 28:15-30; the 12 stones foreshadow the foundations of the New Jerusalem (Rev. 21:19-20)

items.name: Urim and Thummim
items.subtitle: Lights and Perfections — divine oracle
items.description: Mysterious objects placed in the breastplate to consult God. Their exact nature is unknown (stones, dice?). Ourim = 'Lights', Toummim = 'Perfections'. Used to obtain divine answers in important national decisions.

items.name: Large Turban (מִצְנֶפֶת)
items.subtitle: Headdress of the High Priest in fine linen
items.description: Large white linen turban, distinct from the cap of ordinary priests. The gold blade (tsits) is fixed on the turban by a blue cord.

items.name: Golden Blade (צִיץ)
items.subtitle: Gold plaque: 'HOLINESS TO THE LORD'
items.description: Pure gold blade attached to the front of the turban by a blue cord. Engraved with the inscription: 'Qodesh the YHWH' — 'Holiness to the Lord'. The High Priest 'bears' the iniquity of Israel's offerings with this blade.
items.detail: Exodus 28:36-38 — 'that they may find grace before the LORD'
